rationale: Manichaean technical cosmological figure: the Call from the Father of Greatness (Syriac qrīā, Greek κλῆσις) which descends as the apostle's Twin/Companion. Lycopolitan ⲥⲁⲓϣ = ⲥⲁⲡⲥ̄ / ⲥⲱⲡⲥ̄ 'call, summons, supplication.' Capitalize as cosmic principle.

Compound: ϣⲃⲏⲣ ('companion') + ⲁⲟⲩⲏⲧ (= ⲟⲩⲏⲧ 'single, joined, sole'). Designates the unitive Twin-companion (Syzygos) who is bound to the apostle as one — here applied to the Call that comes to the apostle.
Lycopolitan compound ⲣⲙ̄- ('man of') + ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ('light'). Mani's standard self-designation as speaker in the Kephalaia, parallel to but distinct from ⲡⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ 'the Illuminator.'

ⲙⲁ-ⲛ̄-ⲧⲉⲗⲟ = 'place of mounting' from ⲧⲉⲗⲟ 'to mount, ride, embark.' Used in Kephalaion VIII for the Four Mounts which Jesus rode into the world. 'Mount' preserves the verbal-mounting imagery; 'vehicle' is acceptable but less verbal.

Lycopolitan ⲭⲁⲓ — possibly cognate with ϫⲁⲓ 'ship, vessel.' In context 'first mount = ⲡⲭⲁⲓ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ,' the conveyance-semantics suggest 'vessel of light.' Confidence low; could alternatively be 'body' or 'frame.'

Greek loanword βραβεῖον 'prize, victor's award' (cf. Phil 3:14). Standard Manichaean eschatological term for the reward presented to the soul at death by the first of the three angels of the Form of Light.
Headpiece distinct from ⲡⲥⲧⲉⲫⲁⲛⲟⲥ ('wreath') and ⲡⲕⲗⲁⲙ ('crown'). Likely diadem/fillet — the third of the three regalia presented to the soul at death.
Greek loanword θλίψις with Coptic spelling reflecting -ⲗ- elision/assimilation. Paired with κίνδυνοι ('dangers') in standard hardship-doublet (cf. Rom 8:35).
Coptic ⲥⲁⲡ / ⲥⲏⲩ 'turn, season, appointed time.' Used here of the apostle's destined moment of incarnation: 'who comes at the time to bear the church.'
